doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Later Jay & Kai reunions and Kai Winding's death
summary: The electronics album, the Aurex Festival in Japan, and Kai's fatal aneurysm.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You [and Kai] had such a long-running relationship. The group was revisited a number of times. The one you did that had the electronics – I can’t remember which album that was. [It was Betwixt and Between.]
Then you revisited the one where you did Mack the Knife in the two keys.
Oh yeah. Wait a minute. Mack the Knife was with André Previn, wasn’t it?
Yes. That was the two trombones, wasn’t it?
Okay. The two trombone one was the one where you used some of the amplification and stuff – made it more interesting.
Then the last one that you had together with the TV production from . . .
. . . from Switzerland at the Aurex Festival.

The Aurex Festival was Japan. As a matter of fact, it was the most shocking thing. We came back from the Aurex Jazz Festival, and within a matter of a week or ten days I got this call from Kai’s family that he had had a massive brain whatever. I’ve forgotten what it's [called].

Yeah. I couldn’t believe it. I said, "Wait a minute. I just left Kai when he was playing up a storm. as always. What are you telling me?" It was the truth. He had had this massive brain hemorrhage or something like that, as I recall it.
Aneurism. I believe it was an aneurism, a double aneurism. It was very, very
severe. It was devastating news and devastating information to get. He had a tough time of it. He struggled and struggled against this, and finally he succumbed. It was a devastating situation.
